key_insight: The paper presents a fault-tolerant, literature-grounded LLM pipeline that can autonomously move from a large physics corpus to a publishable manuscript while reproducing references, running new computations, and maintaining calibration through external evidence.
engineering_relevance: It demonstrates an architecture for high-stakes scientific automation that relies on fresh-context isolation, distributed grounding, and adversarial review rather than single-agent memory or unverified priors.
method: Mapped 11,083 recent condensed-matter physics arXiv papers to identify a research direction.
Used literature reproduction checkpoints to calibrate methodology before novel first-principles calculations.
Ran the workflow across 47 fresh-context sessions and 6 phases with only on-disk shared state and 2,162 literature-consultation events.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports end-to-end execution on a real corpus, including three substantive physics findings, paired ablations, and quantified intervention/review events that support the grounding mechanism.
watch_item: The approach depends on reliable literature access, reproduction of external references, and bounded human intervention when calibration fails, which may limit portability to less documented or more tool-fragile domains.
paper_title: Grounded autonomous research: a fault-tolerant LLM pipeline from corpus to manuscript in frontier computational physics
